author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Foreign investors returned to net buying of Asian equities in August after nine consecutive months of selling, Reuters reported using LSEG market-flow data.

Investors purchased a net $4.72 billion of shares in Taiwan, South Korea, India, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines during the month. They added another $1.52 billion through Tuesday’s close in September. Those figures are historical snapshots and do not represent live flows.

The shift was concentrated around technology exporters linked to artificial-intelligence spending. Taiwan received $11.15 billion of net inflows in August, while South Korea still recorded an $8.65 billion outflow for a fourth consecutive month. Early September data showed foreign buying returning to both markets.

Corporate results helped improve sentiment: Asian companies beat analyst earnings estimates by an average 10.2% in the latest quarter, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters. Profit growth was 44.7% from a year earlier across the sample, with technology growth at 88.3%. The concentration suggests renewed AI exposure, rather than a uniform return to every Asian market.
dek: LSEG data showed $4.72 billion of net purchases across seven Asian markets in August, led by renewed interest in AI-linked exporters.
headline: Foreign investors return to Asian stocks after nine-month selloff
